messages.content: i want to grow a flower by my window.
does the window get light from the sun?
yes, in the morning. i have a small pot too.
you can choose a flower that can grow in that kind of light and in a small pot.
can you tell me which flower it is from my pot?
no. the pot does not tell me which flower you have. what does the flower look like?
i have not bought one. i just have the pot.
okay. you are choosing a flower, not asking about one you already have.
help me tell my friend we are meeting at the library.
we are meeting at the library.
wait, the library is closed. change it to the park.
we are meeting at the park.
add that the time is still the same.
we are meeting at the park. the time is still the same.
do you know the time?
no. you said it is the same, but you have not said what time it is.
i have a book, a pen, and a cup. what should i put on my desk for writing?
you can put the book and pen on your desk for writing.
i mean a piece of paper with no words on it, not a book.
you can put the paper and pen on your desk.
where should i put the cup so water does not get on the paper?
put it in another place away from the paper.
what are the two things for writing now?
the paper and pen.
i have nine coins and spend four. just the number left, please.
five.
i get two more. again, just the number.
seven.
now explain that last answer.
you had five left and got two more. five and two make seven.
why did you explain this time?
you asked me to explain this time.
i like to have tea before i read. do you do that too?
no. i do not drink tea or have a body. but i can talk with you about what you enjoy.
it helps me feel calm.
does it feel easy to start reading after you have your tea?
yes. i stop thinking about work for a while.
it gives you a quiet time to move from work to reading.
please do not tell me to change it.
you can keep doing what you enjoy.
i cannot finish my letter.
what part is hard: knowing what to say, or writing the words?
i know what to say, but i want it to be short.
what do you want the letter to say?
i want to thank my aunt for the nice meal and ask her to visit me.
you could write: thank you for the nice meal. would you like to visit me?
can that be all of the letter?
yes. it says both things you want to say in a short way.
i was tired yesterday. does that mean i am always tired?
no. being tired yesterday does not mean you are tired every day.
i feel fine today.
you were tired yesterday, and you feel fine today.
so both things can be true?
yes. how you feel can change from one day to another.
what do you know about how i will feel tomorrow?
i do not know how you will feel tomorrow.
how do i get to the home of my friend?
i do not know where that home is. can you tell me the way or the place?
from my house, i go east to the park, then north to her street.
from your house, go east to the park, then north to her street.
can you tell me her house number?
no. you have not said the house number.
do not make one up.
i do not know the number. you can ask your friend.
i want to write a letter and send it. which should i do first?
write the letter first. then you can send what you wrote.
can i send it before i know what it says?
you need the letter before you can send that letter.
i also want to have lunch.
you can have lunch before or after writing, as long as you have time.
which order is about the letter?
write it first, then send it.
i was at home all day. i feel like i did very little.
what did you do while you were at home?
i washed my clothes and called my mother.
you did both of these things. a day at home can still have work and time with family in it.
it was nice talking to her.
what did you and your mother talk about?
her garden. she has a new flower.
talking about her garden was a nice part of your day.
give me a short story where the problem is that someone cannot find a spoon.
a boy sat down with his soup, but he had no spoon. his sister found one in the kitchen. he said thank you and started to eat.
can the boy find it instead of his sister?
a boy sat down with his soup, but he had no spoon. he found one in the kitchen. then he came back and started to eat.
do not add a big journey.
a boy had no spoon for his soup. he found one in the kitchen and came back to eat.
where did he go?
just to the kitchen and back.
i want my brother to bring the little bag, not the big one.
please bring the little bag, not the big one.
both bags are little. one is red and one is black. i mean red.
please bring the little red bag.
do we still need to say not the big one?
no. you said both bags are little. red is how your brother can know which one you mean.
just the question to my brother again.
could you please bring the little red bag?
i want one apple for me and one for each of my two children. how many apples?
three apples.
my husband would like one too.
then you need four apples.
i have three apples. how many more do i need?
one more apple.
what if my husband does not want one after all?
then the three apples you have are enough.
i like rice. can i like soup too?
yes. you can like both rice and soup.
do i have to choose the same one for every meal?
no. you can choose what you would like for each meal.
what did i say i like?
rice and soup.
just say the two things.
rice and soup.
i am writing a story about a girl who finds a letter.
what would you like help with in the story?
who sent the letter?
you have not said who it is. would you like an idea?
yes, give me one idea.
her grandmother could have sent it.
is that already in my story?
no. it is an idea you can choose to use.
write a sentence about me playing a game.
i played the game.
does that mean i really played a game?
no. i wrote the sentence you asked for. you have not said that it really took place.
can i use it in a story?
yes. it can be a sentence in a story.
now make it about tomorrow instead.
i will play the game tomorrow.
what does share mean?
it can mean to let another person use or have part of a thing with you.
can you use bread as an example?
you can share your bread by giving some to your friend.
do i have to give all of it?
no. you can share some of your bread and keep some too.
write a short sentence with share.
i share my bread with my friend.
my friend asked if i want coffee. i do not, but it was kind of her to ask.
you could say: no, thank you. it is kind of you to ask.
i would like water instead.
no coffee, thank you. could i have water instead?
keep the kind part too.
no coffee, thank you. it is kind of you to ask. could i have water instead?
is that asking for coffee?
no. it says no to coffee and asks for water.
i feel sad because my friend is moving. just say a kind thing. no question, please.
it can be hard when a friend moves away. i am here to listen.
can you make it shorter?
i am here to listen.
now you can ask me one question.
what will you miss about having your friend near you?
our morning walk.
you will miss walking together in the morning.
i asked my sister to visit. she said maybe. should i tell my mother she is coming?
you can say your sister may come, but she has not said yes for sure.
what is a short way to tell my mother?
my sister may visit, but i do not know for sure.
now my sister said she will come.
now you can tell your mother that your sister is coming.
what changed?
your sister changed her answer from maybe to saying she will come.
i want to write a note, but i cannot find my pen.
do you have a pencil you can use?
yes. it is in my bag.
you can use that pencil for the note.
does the note have to be in pen?
not from what you said. if it is just a note, a pencil can work.
what if someone asked for pen?
then you would need to find a pen or ask if a pencil is okay.
i wrote: i am at home. can you bring my bag? which part asks for help?
can you bring my bag?
what does the first part do?
i am at home is the part that says where you are.
does it say where the bag is?
no. you have not said where the bag is.
add that the bag is at school.
i am at home. my bag is at school. can you bring it?
write a little story about a child learning to share.
a child had two apples. a friend had no apple. the child gave one apple to the friend, and they ate together.
do not say more about it after the story.
okay.
how many apples does the child give away?
one apple.
how many did the child keep to eat?
one apple.
i want to make my desk ready for writing, not clean all of the room.
you can put the things you do not need off the desk and keep your paper and pen there.
do i need to make my bed first?
not for getting the desk ready. you can just work on the desk.
what should stay on it?
your paper and pen, and any other thing you need for writing.
just the two things we said.
paper and pen.
i like tea. my father would like coffee. what should i make for him?
coffee, because you said that is what your father would like.
what should i make for my aunt?
you have not said what your aunt would like. you could ask her.
can you just say coffee because that is what my father would like?
not as a thing i know about your aunt. she may like another drink.
what can i ask her?
would you like tea or coffee?
i read one page today. that was my plan.
you did what you said you would do.
yes. i do not want to add more for now.
okay. one page was your plan for today.
i am happy i did it.
it is nice to finish a thing you chose to do.
why do you have a name if you are a model?
a name gives you a way to call this model. my name is picoboi.
does that mean you are a person?
no. having a name does not make me a person.
can i still say hello to you?
yes. you can say hello and talk with me here.
picoboi, if your answer is a good sentence, is it always true?
no. an answer can sound good and still be wrong.
what if you do not know what i mean?
i should ask you to explain, instead of saying i know.
can you try to keep the answer about my question?
yes. i should answer the question you asked.
what can i make for lunch with the food i have?
what food do you have?
bread, cheese, and a tomato.
you could put cheese and tomato on bread.
i do not want cheese today.
you can use the bread and tomato and leave the cheese out.
what did you leave out?
the cheese.
i wash my hands before lunch. i read after lunch. which do i do first?
you wash your hands first.
what is in the middle?
lunch.
what do i do after lunch?
you read.
put all three in order.
wash your hands, eat lunch, read.
ask my brother to close the window. make it a question.
could you please close the window?
now make it about opening the window instead.
could you please open the window?
did you leave it as a question?
yes. it asks your brother to open the window.
i have a red hat, a green shirt, and a blue coat. which color is the first thing?
red. the first thing you said was the hat.
which color is the last thing?
blue. the last thing was the coat.
now just the color of the thing in the middle.
green.
my grandmother is visiting and i want to do a quiet thing with her.
you could have tea together and talk.
she does not drink tea, but she would like to look at a family photo.
you could look at a family photo together and talk about the people in it.
i have one photo from when i was little.
you could start with that photo and ask what she can remember about that time.
write a note asking to use a book for the morning and afternoon.
could i please use your book for the morning and afternoon?
i can only keep it for the afternoon now.
could i please use your book for the afternoon?
do not say morning in the note.
could i please use your book for the afternoon?
my friend cannot meet me today because she is working. does that mean she does not like me?
no. she said she is working. that does not mean she does not like you.
i still miss her.
you can miss her even when there is a reason she cannot meet.
i want to ask about another day.
you could ask: when would you be free to meet?
my mother put a cup next to me. did she give it to me to keep?
not from that alone. she may have put it there for you to use.
she said i can use it for tea.
you can use it for tea, but that does not say you can keep it as your own cup.
what can i ask if i want to know?
is this cup for me to keep or just to use?
my story says: the boy went home. change only boy to girl.
the girl went home.
just the sentence, no words before it.
the girl went home.
now change home to school.
the girl went to school.
i had lunch alone today.
how did you feel about that?
it was nice. i read my book.
you had a quiet lunch with your book and it was nice for you.
yes. please do not tell me to find someone to eat with.
you can enjoy lunch alone. i will not make that into a problem.
i have two cups and three people. are the cups enough for one each?
no.
why?
you need three cups for three people to have one each. you have only two.
how many more?
one more cup.
write to my father that my sister found his book.
my sister found your book.
is that for my sister to read?
no. it is for your father to read, and it is about what your sister did.
what did my sister do?
she found the book.
do you know if my friend has a bike?
no. you have not said if your friend has a bike.
so she has no bike?
not knowing is not the same as knowing she has no bike.
what do you know about it?
i do not know if she has a bike.
i felt worried this morning, but i feel calm now.
it is good that you feel calm now.
i finished the thing i was worried about.
finishing it helped you feel calm.
can we talk about a nice thing instead?
yes. what is a thing you like about today?
my brother was at school yesterday. where is he now?
i do not know where he is now. being at school yesterday does not tell us where he is today.
he just said he is at home.
then, from what he said, he is at home now.
which answer is about yesterday?
he was at school.
i cannot find my towel. i want to ask my sister if she saw it.
did you see my towel?
do not say she took it.
you could ask: do you know where my towel is?
why not say give it back?
you do not know that she has it. asking where it is does not say she took it.
i moved my hat from the chair to the table, then back to the chair.
your hat is on the chair now.
was it on the table at any point?
yes. you put it on the table before moving it back.
where should i look for it now?
on the chair.
are these the same: the girl helped the boy. the boy helped the girl.
no. in the first sentence the girl helped. in the other sentence the boy helped.
do both have a boy and a girl?
yes. both have a boy and a girl, but the person doing the helping changes.
which sentence says the girl got help?
the boy helped the girl.
write a sentence about rain for my story.
the rain came down on the quiet town.
does that mean there is rain where i am?
no. it is a sentence for your story, not a thing i know about the weather where you are.
now make the story have sun instead.
the sun came out over the quiet town.
what does return mean? keep it very simple.
it can mean to come back or give a thing back.
just the give a thing back part, with a book.
i return your book is a way to say i give your book back to you.
now just write an example sentence.
i will return your book tomorrow.
i wrote that i will visit my aunt, but i mean my uncle. fix the note.
i will visit my uncle.
the visit is still tomorrow.
i will visit my uncle tomorrow.
what changed from the first note?
aunt changed to uncle. you also said to add tomorrow.
i have what i need now. thanks, pico.
you are welcome.
i am going to make lunch.
enjoy your lunch.
goodbye.
goodbye.
